title: Gravity, Falling Bodies & Projectiles
intro: From Galileo to water rockets: falling, terminal velocity and projectile range, measured in the school field.

lessons.title: The Story of Gravity: Aristotle, Galileo, Newton
lessons.focus: Ideas through history; Leaning Tower thought experiment; hammer-and-feather on the Moon (video or story).
lessons.advanced: Explain Galileo's chained-balls argument against 'heavier falls faster'.

lessons.title: Do Heavy Things Fall Faster? A Fair Test
lessons.focus: Drop stone vs flat paper, then crumpled paper; air resistance confound revealed; same-height release method.
lessons.advanced: Design the test so mass differs but shape does not (bottle + water levels); predict the outcome.

lessons.title: Free Fall and the Acceleration g
lessons.focus: g ≈ 10 m/s² meaning: speed grows 10 m/s each second; velocity table for 0-4 s of fall.
lessons.advanced: Compute speed and distance fallen at t=1,2,3 s using v=gt and d=½gt²; tabulate.

lessons.title: Measuring g: The Pendulum Promise
lessons.focus: Swing period depends on length not mass; preview T=2π√(L/g); plan the experiment (full method in Unit 11).
lessons.advanced: Rearrange T=2π√(L/g) to make g the subject; state what you'll plot.

lessons.title: Measuring g: The Two-Metre Drop
lessons.focus: Drop ball from measured 2 m; three timers average; compute g from d=½gt²; discuss error honestly.
lessons.advanced: Measured time 0.70 s for 2.0 m: compute g, percentage error vs 9.8, and list three error sources ranked.

lessons.title: Terminal Velocity: When Falling Stops Speeding Up
lessons.focus: Drag grows with speed until it balances weight; seeds, raindrops, parachutes; why an ant survives any fall.
lessons.advanced: Use surface-area-to-weight scaling to explain why big animals can't survive falls that insects shrug off.

lessons.title: Designing for Air: Parachute Science
lessons.focus: Canopy area vs fall speed; drop plastic-bag parachutes with stone payload; measure fall time vs area.
lessons.advanced: Plot fall time vs canopy area; fit a trend and extrapolate the area for a 60 kg person (order-of-magnitude).

lessons.title: Egg Drop Challenge I: Design and Build
lessons.focus: Protect a raw egg dropped 3 m using grass, paper, maize cobs, bags; impulse and crumple reasoning before building.
lessons.advanced: Justify your design with impulse: longer stopping time → smaller force (F=Δp/Δt preview).

lessons.title: Egg Drop Challenge II: Test and Autopsy
lessons.focus: Drop from ladder/veranda; inspect damage; correlate failure with design; improve and retest.
lessons.advanced: Estimate impact speed from 3 m (v=√(2gh)); then force for a 0.05 s stop on a 60 g egg.

lessons.title: Throwing Straight Up
lessons.focus: Ball up: slows at g, stops, returns at same speed (no air); time up = time down; catch height symmetry.
lessons.advanced: Total flight 2.4 s: compute launch speed and peak height using symmetry.

lessons.title: How High Did It Go? Energy Preview
lessons.focus: Estimate peak from flight time; KE→PE story; measure throw heights off a marked wall.
lessons.advanced: Equate ½mv²=mgh to show h=v²/2g; find launch speed for a 5 m mango-branch clearance.

lessons.title: Projectile Motion I: Sideways and Down Are Independent
lessons.focus: Roll ball off table while dropping another: same landing time; horizontal steady + vertical accelerates.
lessons.advanced: Ball leaves 1.25 m table at 3.0 m/s: compute flight time and range.

lessons.title: Projectile Motion II: Angle and Range
lessons.focus: Throw stones at measured angles; 45° wins (no air); 30° and 60° tie; javelin angle reality ~35°.
lessons.advanced: Explain with range formula R=v²sin2θ/g why 45° maximizes range; why do javelin throwers use less?

lessons.title: The Water Rocket Project I: Pressure and Design
lessons.focus: Bottle + water + air pressure = rocket; action-reaction and momentum preview; fin/nose design drawings.
lessons.advanced: Sketch forces on the rocket at launch: thrust, weight, drag; when is acceleration greatest?

lessons.title: The Water Rocket Project II: Build Day
lessons.focus: Construct fins, nose cone, payload bay; check symmetry and straight flight path; launcher safety briefing.
lessons.advanced: Compute centre of pressure vs centre of gravity positions; why must CG lead CP for stable flight?

lessons.title: The Water Rocket Project III: Launch and Measure
lessons.focus: Vary water fill (1/4, 1/3, 1/2) and launch angle; measure range and flight time; crown the champion with data.
lessons.advanced: From flight time and angle, estimate launch speed; explain the optimum fill fraction using mass vs impulse.

lessons.title: Physics of Kenyan Athletics
lessons.focus: Julius Yego's javelin angles, Eliud Kipchoge's pacing (steady speed = efficiency); analyze race splits from data cards.
lessons.advanced: Kipchoge: 42.195 km in 2:01:09 — compute average speed and per-km pace; compare with your dash.

lessons.title: Orbits and Satellites: Falling Around the Earth
lessons.focus: Throw harder and farther until you orbit; Kenya's space milestones (Uhuru-1, Taifa-1) and why satellites don't fall.
lessons.advanced: Explain weightlessness in orbit as continuous free fall, not absence of gravity.

lessons.title: The Coin and Feather Problem
lessons.focus: Attempt near-vacuum demo in a bottle with pump; failing that, reason from parachute data: without air, all fall together.
lessons.advanced: Write the argument that closes the case even if the demo is imperfect: what evidence settles it?

lessons.title: Unit Review: Gravity Games
lessons.focus: Stations: drop timing, parachute race, projectile range, egg-drop finals; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Combined problem: a stone thrown horizontally at 8 m/s from a 20 m cliff — time, range, impact speed.
